blocking_review.body:
## :x: BLOCKING REVIEW / not ready for approval yet.

Review record: PR #432 / Issue #181
Exact head: `4d66946a2b05e4588892356cbcf7a623e9fa4527`
Declared base: `release/0.1.0-r2`
Review timestamp: 2026-08-25T16:01:01Z
Review ID: `pr-432-4d66946a2b05-1787673487029-86301288`

### 1. Issue and evidence fully inspected
Read the complete Issue and inspect all evidence before judging the implementation.

- [x] The complete canonical Issue was read, including body, acceptance criteria, comments, links, and dependencies.
  > The complete Issue #181 body, acceptance criteria, deployment contract, historical note, dependencies, current PR delta, comments, and CI evidence were inspected.
- [x] Every Issue attachment or linked evidence artifact was inspected, including screenshots, videos, and comparison references.
  > No Issue attachments were present; the linked historical PR/review evidence and current packaged/demo acceptance claims were inspected.
- [x] Related Issues, parent/ancestor PRs, and existing accepted behavior were inspected where relevant.
  > The prior query-gated first-demo implementation, current demo profile code, deployment helper, filesystem seed authority, and current test inventory were inspected.

### 2. Issue intent, scope, and protected behavior understood
Identify the user problem and intended observable behavior independently of the PR description.

- [x] The user problem and desired observable behavior were stated independently of the PR implementation.
  > The user need is a real demo deployment with representative files/shortcuts, not URL-triggered test fixtures, while local packaging stays clean.
- [x] Protected behavior, explicit non-goals, and compatibility boundaries were identified.
  > The protected boundaries are the existing package-profile/deployment seam, canonical FsService seed/reconciliation, stable NodeId shortcuts, local non-demo behavior, and separate #121 game ownership.
- [ ] The PR scope matches the Issue intent rather than a narrower or implementation-defined substitute.
  > :x: The PR adds the profile path but leaves the old live first-demo query seed path in apps/plasmon/src/index.tsx and firstDemoFixture.ts, contrary to Issue #181's one-demo-mode/no-query contract.

### 3. Release policy and integration context verified
Check release-specific authority, declared bases, stacked dependencies, and which parent work is actually creditable.

- [x] Current assignment, release policy, target branch, and package/version constraints were read.
  > The target is release/0.1.0-r2; release/package guidance and the Plasmon package-profile/deployment constraints were inspected.
- [x] The declared PR base, stacked-parent relationship, and integration assumptions were verified.
  > The declared base and exact head 4d66946a2b05e4588892356cbcf7a623e9fa4527 were verified, including the current-r2 integration history.
- [x] Only merged or otherwise explicitly creditable parent behavior was counted as implemented.
  > Existing filesystem authority and deployment infrastructure were counted as parent behavior; the reviewed additions were limited to profile/content wiring, tests, and docs.

### 4. Implementation correctness and failure paths verified
Review success, failure, boundary, asynchronous, cancellation, cleanup, and regression behavior—not only the happy path.

- [x] Success, failure, empty, exceptional, and boundary paths were inspected where applicable.
  > The production path covers demo/non-demo profile selection, seeded files, shortcut reconciliation, package archive preparation, and normal FileManager/Search/association opening.
- [x] Async ownership, cancellation, teardown, cleanup, error visibility, and resource ownership were inspected where applicable.
  > Demo startup awaits filesystem readiness before shortcut reconciliation; the deployment helper resets inherited profile state for Plasmon and awaits packaging/provision commands.
- [x] The change does not materially regress unrelated accepted behavior.
  > Fast, packaged local specialist, persistence, smoke, Review, Kernel, and flake contexts passed; the concrete failures are acceptance-contract gaps rather than an observed unrelated regression.

### 5. Architecture, authority, and subsystem boundaries preserved
Confirm that behavior remains in the canonical owning layer and does not create parallel authority or cross a product boundary.

- [x] The canonical owning service, model, controller, or adapter remains authoritative.
  > Package profile selection remains in the build/deployment boundary, filesystem seeds use existing bootstrap/reconciliation, and shortcuts use nodeShortcutSeedSpec/readSharedShortcut.
- [x] Relevant identity, filesystem, Neutron, Process, Windowing, Shell, security, or other subsystem boundaries remain intact.
  > Stable filesystem NodeIds, Desktop shortcut identity, Process/association opening, Neutron package profile, and separate game fixture ownership remain distinct.
- [x] No duplicate authority, hidden parallel implementation, or convenience architecture was introduced.
  > No new filesystem database or shortcut format is introduced; the demo content is translated into existing seed and shared-shortcut primitives.

### 6. Tests are honest, deterministic, and sufficient
Tests must observe production behavior at the lowest truthful layer and must not be weakened or made circular.

- [x] Tests assert user-visible or contract behavior rather than source shape, incidental structure, or constants alone.
  > The model tests assert asset bytes, seed metadata, local absence, shortcut targets, Search classification, and native handlers; the browser test asserts actual installed UI behavior.
- [x] Tests use the lowest honest layer with deterministic control and appropriate negative/boundary cases.
  > Deterministic seed/deployment tests use MemoryFs and production composition, while packaged UI claims use Playwright; the missing demo execution owner is separately identified.
- [x] Fixtures, examples, tolerances, and bounds match the Issue rather than being relaxed to fit the implementation.
  > Repository assets are concrete Markdown/SVG files and tests assert representative structure and exact UTF-8 bytes without relaxed source-shape-only claims.

### 7. Runtime, packaged, browser, and manual evidence verified
Use real packaged/browser/manual evidence whenever the claim depends on layout, assets, runtime, persistence, or visual parity.

- [x] The required evidence layer for the Issue was identified correctly.
  > The deployment/profile and filesystem claims are tested below React, but Issue #181 explicitly requires a real packaged demo preparation and browser acceptance boundary.
- [ ] Packaged, browser, runtime, persistence, or human/manual evidence was inspected where the claim requires it.
  > :x: The current CI contexts run local Specialist, smoke, persistence, Review, and Kernel lanes; no checked-in workflow invokes plasmon:demo:prepare plus test:e2e:plasmon:demo, and the demo spec is skipped outside the demo manifest.
- [x] Execution evidence is distinguished from CI status and is not replaced by a green status label.
  > Green CI was inspected as execution evidence, and its absence of the demo workflow was distinguished from the passing ordinary packaged lanes.

### 8. Compatibility, regressions, documentation, and release obligations reviewed
Check durable state, compatibility, scope, documentation, generated artifacts, and applicable release obligations.

- [x] Durable state, persistence, migration, serialized contracts, and upgrade/restart behavior were reviewed where applicable.
  > The change adds no persistent schema or migration; demo seeds/shortcuts are ordinary filesystem data reconciled through existing durable seed behavior.
- [x] Required architecture, API, developer-facing, persistence, or integration documentation was reviewed or updated where applicable.
  > Demo, frontend, application, and integration documentation markers were refreshed, and their descriptions match the new profile/content path.
- [x] Scope, generated artifacts, dependency changes, release obligations, and unrelated work were reviewed.
  > The changed files are task-related profile/build/content/deployment/test/docs files; no generated archive or dependency update was added.

### 9. Exact-head and reviewer-operational disposition verified
The formal disposition must be bound to the current exact head and must follow reviewer independence and reporting rules.

- [x] The exact PR head and declared base were recorded and refreshed immediately before output.
  > The exact head/base were recorded from the complete bundle and refreshed immediately before submission; queue still reports PR #432 COMPLETE at 4d66946a2b05e4588892356cbcf7a623e9fa4527.
- [x] The reviewer did not implement product changes, merge, force-push, or alter another agent's work.
  > The reviewer performed read-only research and review submission only; it did not modify product code, merge, force-push, or alter another worktree.
- [x] CI status and failures are recorded as merge/infrastructure evidence, not used as product-correctness proof.
  > All listed CI contexts and flake iterations passed, but the missing demo execution and legacy query path remain substantive acceptance blockers.

### 10. Acceptance criteria represented in production code and tests
Every Issue acceptance criterion must have production implementation and at least one honest executable test in this PR or an already-merged or pending-merge parent branch. Each criterion below comes directly from the linked Issue.

- [x] `npm run plasmon:demo:prepare` produces a Plasmon package that seeds the three representative document/media resources on a fresh demo filesystem without URL/query rewriting.
  > The demo deployment helper selects the demo profile internally and the build embeds asset bytes into the Plasmon package; the separate packaged execution gap is recorded under criterion 13.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > packageProfileForDeployment returns demo only for the demo manifest/Plasmon workspace, build.ts embeds the three assets, and index.tsx seeds/reconciles them for isDemoProfile.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts and the demo Playwright spec cover seed composition and installed behavior, although the packaged spec lacks a required CI owner.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The tests inspect MemoryFs/production composition and rendered installed resources, not only source constants.

- [x] `Demo Guide.md` is a real repository `.md` asset with representative Markdown structure, and the seeded bytes exactly match that file.
  > Demo Guide.md is a repository asset with representative Markdown and demoContent tests compare its exact bytes with seed bytes.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > build.ts reads Demo Guide.md from apps/plasmon/src/demo/assets and demoContent.ts receives the packaged content rather than an independent inline document.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts asserts headings, task list, table, code fence, and exact seeded UTF-8 equality with readFileSync content.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Assertions inspect actual asset contents and generated seed bytes.

- [x] `Demo Artwork.svg` is a real standalone repository `.svg` asset, and the seeded bytes exactly match that file.
  > Demo Artwork.svg is a standalone repository asset and its seed bytes are compared exactly.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > build.ts embeds the repository SVG and demoContent.ts assigns it image/svg+xml through the production seed spec.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The deterministic test validates XML/SVG structure and exact seed-byte equality, and the packaged demo journey opens the artwork in Photos.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test observes file contents/structure and installed Photos rendering rather than only checking a filename.

- [x] All three demo files have Desktop shortcuts on a fresh demo filesystem.
  > reconcileDemoDesktopShortcuts creates three shared shortcut seed specs after filesystem readiness, and deterministic tests verify three entries.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > index.tsx awaits services.filesystem.ready before calling reconcileDemoDesktopShortcuts, which creates one spec per demo resource.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts invokes reconciliation twice and asserts exactly three matching Desktop entries; the packaged demo test observes all three Desktop entries.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The tests inspect actual FsService Desktop listings and installed FileManager nodes.

- [x] Desktop shortcuts target the real demo resources by stable NodeId through the shared shortcut model.
  > nodeShortcutSeedSpec resolves target paths to stable NodeIds and readSharedShortcut assertions verify the canonical target metadata.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The shortcut specs use targetPath and the existing shared nodeShortcutSeedSpec, not path strings persisted as shortcut targets.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts compares each shortcut's readSharedShortcut result with the corresponding resource NodeId.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The assertion uses production shortcut decoding and actual resource IDs.

- [x] Demo files and shortcuts are created through production filesystem/bootstrap/reconciliation seams and are idempotent.
  > Demo files flow through createPlasmonServices/bootstrap and shortcuts through reconcileSeedManifest; calling reconciliation twice is covered.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > createDemoSeeds returns ordinary FilesystemSeedSpec entries and reconcileDemoDesktopShortcuts delegates to existing filesystem seed authority.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The composition test runs production MemoryFs-backed services and calls reconciliation twice.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Tests observe stable counts/targets and opening outcomes rather than reproducing reconciliation policy.

- [x] FileManager, Search, Desktop activation, and native associations can discover/open the resources normally.
  > The headless composition covers FileManager-relevant resources through Search, Desktop shortcut activation, and native associations; the packaged demo journey covers installed UI discovery/opening when explicitly run.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The production seed content is ordinary filesystem data and opening remains the existing Search/association/process path.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts asserts Search categories, association handler IDs, and opening through shortcut IDs; the packaged spec covers Desktop, FileManager, Search, Text, Markdown, and Photos.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The tests observe production service/process records and rendered installed windows/resources.

- [x] Ordinary `neutron-plasmon` packaging and the bounded `plasmon:local:*` deployment remain free of these #181 demo seeds by default.
  > isDemoProfile gates new demo seeds, and ordinary composition tests verify the demo paths are absent without demoSeeds.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > packageProfileForDeployment only sets demo for the demo manifest and packageEnvironmentForDeployment deletes an inherited profile before selecting it.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts verifies ordinary createPlasmonServices composition has no demo files or Desktop names.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The absence assertions inspect resolved paths and actual Desktop listings.

- [x] `plasmon:demo:prepare` continues to use the existing Plasmon `package` command; no additional `package:demo` npm operation is required.
  > prepareDeploymentEnvironment always runs the existing workspace package script and only injects the profile through its environment for the demo Plasmon workspace.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The helper invokes npm --workspace neutron-plasmon run package; no package:demo script is added.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The deployment test verifies the existing package command in the resolved artifact workspace and the package scripts expose the normal deployment commands.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The code/test inspect command selection semantics rather than merely asserting an archive exists.

- [x] Callers do not have to provide a new environment variable to obtain demo behavior; `plasmon:demo:prepare` supplies the existing package-profile context internally.
  > The public plasmon:demo:prepare script selects the demo manifest and the coordinator supplies PLASMON_PACKAGE_PROFILE=demo internally.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > packageEnvironmentForDeployment constructs the child environment, removes any inherited profile, and sets demo only for the demo Plasmon workspace.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The public scope scripts and deployment tests exercise scope selection without requiring callers to set the profile variable.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The tested behavior is deployment command selection, not source-shape inspection.

- [x] Demo assets have clear redistribution provenance.
  > The repository-owned text/Markdown/SVG assets and README provenance statements provide clear redistribution provenance.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Assets are checked into apps/plasmon/src/demo/assets and build.ts reads those files directly.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts reads each repository asset and compares the seeded bytes exactly.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test checks actual asset structure and exact bytes.

- [x] Game fixture behavior remains composed through #121 rather than duplicated.
  > The PR's new demo content excludes /Games and the demo README explicitly leaves game/runtime fixture ownership to Issue #121.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > createDemoSeeds contains only Documents/Pictures and three files; it does not define game resources or runtime behavior.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts asserts no seed has parentPath /Games.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test observes the seed manifest content and parent paths.

- [x] Deterministic tests prove demo-vs-local selection and filesystem/shortcut behavior at the lowest truthful layer.
  > Deterministic tests cover local/demo manifest selection, package profile selection, exact asset bytes, seed/reconciliation, shortcuts, Search, and associations.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The deployment helper and demo content modules implement the required profile and filesystem behavior through existing seams.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > demoContent.test.ts and plasmon-deployment-environment.test.ts provide executable low-layer coverage for the listed behavior.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Tests use MemoryFs/production services and actual repository files rather than duplicating filesystem policy.

- [ ] Packaged/demo acceptance verifies the actual `plasmon:demo` preparation path rather than injecting browser state.
  > :x: The packaged/demo acceptance spec exists and has an explicit npm command, but no checked-in workflow in the current head runs plasmon:demo:prepare, demo provisioning, and test:e2e:plasmon:demo; ordinary Specialist explicitly excludes the profile-specific spec.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The production deployment helper, demo package script, and demo Playwright command are present.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: Current workflow inspection found no demo browser workflow; the required CI contexts run local Specialist/smoke/persistence paths, while the spec is skipped unless NEUTRON_NDEPLOY_CONFIG is plasmon.ndeploy.json.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The demo spec itself asserts installed behavior, but no current execution evidence proves that the actual demo preparation path ran it.

### Summary
> Approval is allowed only when every checkbox above is checked. CI status is recorded separately and is not used as proof that the Issue is solved.
